fixes.explanation: A sheep-shearing feast isn't what this verse names. The women invited the men to the sacrifices for their gods (Numbers 25:2). That detail matters, because the verse goes on to say the people ate and bowed down to those gods.

Judges, yes. Moses told "…the judges of Israel…" and gave them the order: "Each of you must kill all of his men who have joined in worshiping Baal of Peor." (Numbers 25:5). Each judge is handed the job for his own men. I think that's a heavy thing to be asked to carry.

Priests aren't the ones Moses speaks to here. He tells "…the judges of Israel…" (Numbers 25:5). Aaron the priest comes up a couple of verses later, named as Phinehas's grandfather (Numbers 25:7). But the order in this verse goes to the judges.

Soldiers would make sense for a hard order like this. But the verse names a different group: Moses told "…the judges of Israel…" (Numbers 25:5). Soldiers aren't mentioned in it. The judges are the ones given the order.

Not quite, friend. Verse 9 says, "…those who died in the plague numbered 24,000." It's a big number, and it's easy to mix up. This is one of the heaviest lines in the chapter, so I think it's worth pausing on.

Yes, baker. The LORD says Phinehas "…was zealous for My sake among them, so that I did not consume the Israelites in My zeal." (Numbers 25:11). Zealous means burning with devotion. The LORD says it was "for My sake," so He is the one Phinehas's zeal was for. The LORD even uses the same word, zeal, for Himself in that verse.

A city isn't the gift in this verse. The LORD says, "Declare, therefore, that I am granting him My covenant of peace." (Numbers 25:12). The gift is a covenant, and no city is named. I think a word like peace is a welcome one after a chapter this heavy.

It's actually true, baker. The LORD says, "It will be a covenant of permanent priesthood for him and his descendants…" (Numbers 25:13). The word is permanent, and it reaches his descendants too. So the LORD is describing a gift that goes beyond Phinehas himself.

Yes, friend. The LORD says Phinehas "…was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites." (Numbers 25:13). Atonement is the word for making things right with God. In the same speech, the LORD says Phinehas turned His wrath away from the Israelites (Numbers 25:11). Both of those were done for the people.

No altar is built in this passage. The LORD says Phinehas "…was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites." (Numbers 25:13). Atonement is the word for making things right with God, and the LORD says Phinehas did that for the Israelites. The same speech says Phinehas turned the LORD's wrath away from them (Numbers 25:11).

Prayer is a good thing, but this passage never has Phinehas leading one. The LORD says he "…was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites." (Numbers 25:13). Atonement is the word for making things right with God. The LORD says Phinehas did that for the Israelites, and that he turned His wrath away from them (Numbers 25:11).
